summary.text: The value 67 has at least two distinct preimages: the relevant residue sums for \(m=147\) and \(m=2055\) are respectively \(1+3+3+3+19+19+19=67\) and \(1+3+9\cdot 7=67\). Hence its number of occurrences is at least two, contradicting the claimed value one.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
F(m)=\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor \log_2 m\rfloor} (m\bmod 2^k)
\]
be sequence A049802. Thus A383327 is the multiplicity function
\[
a(n)=\#\{m:F(m)=n\}.
\]
In the precise finite formulation of the conjecture, for every positive \(n\) this is computed as the cardinality of
\[
T_n=\{m:0\le m<2^{n+1}\text{ and }F(m)=n\};
\]
the bound \(2^{n+1}\) is sufficient for all occurrences of the positive value \(n\). For the disproof below it is enough merely to exhibit two distinct members of \(T_{67}\).

We use the two indices
\[
m_1=147\qquad\text{and}\qquad m_2=2055.
\]
We first calculate \(F(147)\). Since
\[
2^7=128\le 147<256=2^8,
\]
we have \(\lfloor\log_2 147\rfloor=7\), so precisely the moduli \(2,4,8,16,32,64,128\) occur in the sum. Their remainders are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
2^k&2&4&8&16&32&64&128\\ \hline
147\bmod 2^k&1&3&3&3&19&19&19.
\end{array}
\]
Indeed, the first four entries follow from \(147=146+1=144+3\), while for the last three we use \(147=128+19\); the relevant multiples subtracted are respectively \(128,128,128\), and \(19\) is smaller than each of \(32,64,128\). Consequently
\[
F(147)=1+3+3+3+19+19+19=10+57=67.
\]
Thus \(147\) is one occurrence of the value \(67\) in A049802.

Next calculate \(F(2055)\). We have
\[
2^{11}=2048\le2055<4096=2^{12},
\]
so \(\lfloor\log_2 2055\rfloor=11\). Also
\[
2055=2048+7=2^{11}+7.
\]
For \(k=1\), the remainder modulo \(2\) is \(1\), and for \(k=2\), the remainder modulo \(4\) is \(3\). For every \(k\) with \(3\le k\le11\), the number \(2^k\) divides \(2^{11}=2048\), while \(0\le7<2^k\). Therefore
\[
2055\bmod 2^k=7\qquad(3\le k\le11).
\]
There are \(11-3+1=9\) such indices. Hence
\[
F(2055)=1+3+9\cdot7=4+63=67.
\]
Thus \(2055\) is a second occurrence of the value \(67\) in A049802.

The two indices are distinct, since \(147\ne2055\). They also both lie in the range used to define \(a(67)\): certainly
\[
147<2055<2^{12}<2^{68}=2^{67+1}.
\]
It follows that both \(147\) and \(2055\) belong to
\[
T_{67}=\{m<2^{68}:F(m)=67\}.
\]
A finite set containing two distinct elements has cardinality at least two. Therefore
\[
a(67)=\#T_{67}\ge2,
\]
and in particular
\[
a(67)\ne1.
\]

Finally, \(67\) is one of the explicitly listed values in
\[
S=\{1,3,5,9,15,23,35,63,65,67\}.
\]
The conjecture asserts that every \(n\in S\) satisfies \(a(n)=1\). Applying that assertion to the member \(67\in S\) would give \(a(67)=1\), contradicting the inequality just proved. Hence the conjecture is false.
